 Quick answers 

## What people ask first.

## Who builds websites in Sevenoaks?

 Conversion Forge is one person, Tk, based in Sevenoaks, Kent. I build websites, local SEO and lead generation for small businesses across the UK and abroad, with clients in Canada and South Africa. 

## How much does a website cost?

 £175 is the minimum, for a simple website; the price goes up with the number of pages and what the site needs to do. The Starter package, with a Google Business Profile and local SEO foundations added, is £495. No monthly fee is needed to keep a site live. 

## How long does it take?

 Most service business websites go live in under 72 hours. A full online shop takes about two weeks. 

## Do I own the website?

 Yes. The code, the content, the domain and the accounts are handed over to you. 

## Which areas do you cover?

 Anywhere. I am based in Sevenoaks and work with businesses across Kent, London and the rest of the UK, and remotely abroad: a Pilates studio in Toronto and a software platform for a business in South Africa.

# About Tk · Founder of Conversion Forge
URL: https://conversionforge.co.uk/about.html

About Tk · Founder of Conversion Forge 

 About 

## One person.Sevenoaks, Kent.

 Conversion Forge is not an agency floor. It is me, Tk, and a stack of systems I built so that a small business can get the same machinery a big one buys, without the monthly bill. 

 Who you are dealing with 

## There is no account manager.There is just me.

 Tk · Founder · Sevenoaks, Kent 

 My name is Tk. I was born in South Africa and I live in Sevenoaks. I left my job in pursuit of a way to be a more present father while still providing for my family, and to find the work life balance I actually wanted. The reward I get is giving small businesses prices they can afford at the level they are at right now. 

 I kept seeing the same thing. The word of mouth well tends to dry up, and the local business tends to miss out on making the most of its online reputation to get attention. So I set out to give small businesses the best way to contend with big businesses and even bigger budgets. Nothing I build is out of range, and you do not do it alone. 

 When you talk to Conversion Forge, you are talking to me. I answer the first message, I run the discovery call, I build the thing, and I am the one you shout at if it breaks. There is no team to hide behind and no junior learning on your money. 

 The work 

## Built once. Handed over.Yours to keep.

 Most agencies rent you a website. Stop paying, and it goes dark. I build the system, put your name on it, and give you the keys: the code, the accounts, the passwords, the lot. If you never speak to me again, everything I built keeps running. 

 The work itself is unglamorous and specific. Getting a business to show up on Google Maps when someone nearby is searching for it. Building a site that turns a visitor into a booking instead of an award. Rewriting an eBay listing so it actually gets found. Setting up the outreach that fills a quiet week. 

 I use a lot of automation to do it, which is why the prices are what they are. That is the honest reason. It is not magic and I am not going to dress it up as magic. 

 Who I have built for 

## Real businesses.Most of them down the road.

 A barber shop in Sevenoaks. A personal trainer. A car dealer. A Jamaican restaurant. A jewellery seller doing 240 product variations on eBay. These are not logos I bought the right to display. They are people whose sites I built and whose numbers I can show you, and several of them are a short walk from my front door. 

 The numbers on the case studies come from the platforms that produced them, not from a spreadsheet I made up. If a figure cannot be traced back to Search Console, eBay Seller Hub, or Instagram Insights, it does not go on the page. 

 Some of the work did not go to plan, and where that happened I say so on the case study rather than quietly leaving it out. An agency that has never had a bad month is an agency that is lying to you. 

 How I work 

## Four things I will not move on.

 You own it. Every engagement ends with a handover folder. Source code, content, accounts, credentials. No hostage situations. 

 No retainer unless you want one. You pay for a thing, you get the thing. If you want me to keep improving it afterwards, that is a separate conversation and it is your choice, not a condition. 

 Every number is traceable. If I cannot show you where a figure came from, I will not use it. 

 I tell you when something will not work. Including when the thing you are asking me to sell you is the wrong thing to buy. I would rather lose the sale than build you something that quietly fails for a year. 

 Next step 

## Have a look at your own businessthe way Google sees it.

 The free audit is exactly what it says. I look at what a customer finds when they search for a business like yours, and I tell you where you are losing the job. There is no obligation and no sales sequence waiting on the other side of it. 

 If it turns out you do not need me, I will say that too. 

 Book a free call

# Methodology · How Conversion Forge Builds Marketing Systems
URL: https://conversionforge.co.uk/methodology.html

Methodology · How Conversion Forge Builds Marketing Systems 

 Methodology 

## Six engines.One system.

 How Conversion Forge ships systems instead of retainers. The architecture, the model stack, and the principle behind every deliverable being owned by the client. 

 The Architecture 

## Six engines, sequenced.

 Each engine is a distinct workflow. Specialisation means each ships fast and breaks less. Failure in one engine does not cascade to the others. 

 Engine 01 
 Intake and qualification 
 Onboarding form, discovery call, prospect-fit classification. Sorts in scope from out of scope before money changes hands. 

 Engine 02 
 Proposal generation 
 Three modes (priced-stages, discovery, tier-2 multi-phase). Brand-cohered, dual-emit markdown plus HTML, humanizer-checked. 

 Engine 03 
 Demo build 
 Cloudflare Pages site, brand-cohered theme, shared chassis components. Live URL the client can hand to a friend. 

 Engine 04 
 Lead and revenue rails 
 Stripe checkout, contact forms, callback widgets, automated outreach. The plumbing that turns visits into revenue. 

 Engine 05 
 SEO and AI visibility 
 Schema markup, llms.txt, structured data. Local pack ranking and citation across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity. 

 Engine 06 
 Handover and ownership 
 Branded PDF recap, OneDrive folder, every credential and source file. The client owns it from day one. 

 How the work is made 

## The best mind for the job.Then a second to check it.

 Most of what calls itself AI is a single model doing everything. That is the quick way, and it shows in the work. We do the slower, more deliberate thing. Every part of your project is given to the system best suited to it, and the parts that matter are checked by a separate one that played no part in making them. More passes, more scrutiny, and a result that holds up when it counts. 

 The right intelligence for each task 
 Planning, writing, building and reviewing each call for a different kind of thinking. Every step of your work is matched to the system best suited to it, rather than forced through one tool that is only ever passable at all of them. 

 A second opinion on everything that matters 
 Important work is checked by a separate, independent system that had no part in making it. One mind can be confidently wrong. Two rarely make the same mistake. By the time the work reaches you, it has already been challenged. 

 It keeps running when one part fails 
 The method never leans on a single supplier. If one is busy or unavailable, the work carries on and you never see the difference. Your pipeline does not have an off switch. 

 One standard, every time 
 Whichever part of the system does the work, the bar is the same. You get the considered version, planned, drafted and checked, not the first thing a machine happened to return. 

 Questions clients ask 

## Before you book.

 Why does Conversion Forge use six engines instead of one? 
 Each engine is a distinct workflow with its own LLM model, its own data sources, and its own success criteria. Lead generation runs on a different rhythm than payment integration, which runs differently from SEO. Specialising the engines means each one ships faster and breaks less than a single monolithic system would. Failure in one engine does not cascade to the others. 

 What powers the systems? 
 More than one system, and never only one. Different work calls for different strengths, so each task is given to the approach best suited to it, and the parts that matter are checked by a separate, independent one. We are not tied to any single provider, which is also why the work keeps running if one of them has a bad day. 

 Do clients own what we build? 
 Yes. Every engagement closes with a handover bundle: source code, content, accounts, and credentials, in a folder the client owns. The agency retains internal operating systems, but the client never has to come back to us to make a change. If we ever stop trading, the client keeps running. 

 What does the 72-hour build claim actually mean? 
 It means the core lead-generation system (Google Business Profile, contact form, basic site, first outreach sequence) is configured and live within 72 hours of the initial discovery call. It does not mean every long-term growth lever is in place. Those layer in over weeks two through six. 

 How do you measure success? 
 Platform-verifiable numbers only. Impressions and conversion rates come from Google Search Console, eBay Seller Hub, Instagram Insights, or the client's own analytics. The case study page publishes screenshots, not estimates. If a number cannot be sourced from the platform that generated it, it does not get used. 

 Who do you work with? 
 Small businesses in the UK and abroad: tradespeople, restaurants, studios and online shops. The same method is also delivered remotely, for example a Pilates studio in Toronto and a software platform for a business in South Africa. It is one person doing the work, so a project is only taken on when it can be delivered well. 

 Your Business 

## See it in your context.

 Book a free 30-minute strategy call. We'll show you exactly which engines your business needs and which ones it does not. 

 Book Free Strategy Call

 WhatsApp

# Web Design for Small Businesses · UK and Worldwide · Conversion Forge
URL: https://conversionforge.co.uk/services/web-design-sevenoaks-kent

Web Design for Small Businesses · UK and Worldwide · Conversion Forge 

 Service 

## A website you own. Built in Sevenoaks. Live in days, not months.

 Websites for small businesses in the UK and worldwide: built once, handed over, yours to keep. Booking, ordering and search foundations included. From £175. Get the free audit or email Tk Based in Sevenoaks Handed over, yours to keep Kent, London and further conversionforge.co.uk/services Illustration, generated for this site £175 from, for a website you own outright 72 hours or less to live, for the entry website 20 checks every site passes before it goes live 01 

## Why the ownership matters more than the design

 Most small-business websites are rented. The agency holds the domain, the code sits on their platform, and the monthly fee is what keeps the lights on. Stop paying and the site goes dark. That arrangement suits the agency, not the business. I build the site once and hand it over. You own the code, the content and the domain, and no retainer is required to keep it live. If you ever want someone else to work on it, you take it with you. There is no account manager here. Conversion Forge is one person, me, Tk, working from Sevenoaks in Kent. The person you email is the person who builds the site. 02 

## What every site I build ships with, on day one

 The search foundations are not an upgrade. They ship with the site the day it goes live, because a site nobody can find is a brochure in a drawer. Every site carries a sitemap.xml, a robots.txt that names all 15 AI and search crawlers by name, and llms.txt plus llms-full.txt so an AI assistant asked about your business can read the facts straight from you. Every page carries JSON-LD schema: the business, the breadcrumbs, and the questions and answers where a page has them. Open Graph and Twitter cards are set so a shared link shows a proper card. Canonical tags are set so the right page gets the credit. Images carry their dimensions, which is a small thing that stops them vanishing on iPhones. Legal pages are included. The build is mobile-first, because that is where most of your visitors are. Before any site goes live it passes a 20-check ship gate. I wrote that gate from real client incidents, one check per thing that once went wrong, so the same mistake cannot ship twice. 03 

## Work you can look at

 Chaplins Barbers, 41 Dartford Road, Sevenoaks. Their site says established 1889, which is the year Charles Chaplin was born, and voted best barber in Sevenoaks. Skin fades, scissor cuts and hot towel shaves, with bookings by WhatsApp. Live at chaplinsofsevenoaks.co.uk , a single-fee engagement, handed over. Jerkeez 876, 73 London Road, Sevenoaks. Jamaican and Caribbean food with the menu online and pre-order for collection. Live at jerkeez.co.uk . The 876 is Jamaica's dialling code, which I noticed before I wrote a word of their copy. # Local SEO and AI Search Visibility for Small Businesses · Conversion Forge
URL: https://conversionforge.co.uk/services/local-seo-ai-search-visibility

Local SEO and AI Search Visibility for Small Businesses · Conversion Forge 

 Service 

## Be the answer when your town searches. On Google, and now in ChatGPT.

 Local SEO for small businesses: Google Business Profile, the local pack, schema, llms.txt and AI-search citation. Built to be found without paid ads. Get the free audit or email Tk Based in Sevenoaks Handed over, yours to keep Kent, London and further conversionforge.co.uk/services Illustration, generated for this site 15 AI crawlers named in every robots file I ship 71,583 views for a Sevenoaks restaurant in 29 days £0 spent on ads to reach them 01 

## Two search results now, not one

 When someone in Sevenoaks looks for a barber, a grill or a Pilates instructor, the search happens in two places. One is the Google local pack, the map with three names under it. The other is an AI answer, in ChatGPT, Gemini or Perplexity, that names one or two businesses and moves on. A site can be built to be cited by both. The same facts, laid out so a person can read them and a machine can read them too. That is the whole of what I do here, and it does not require paid ads. The honest part first. Rankings take weeks to move, and nobody can promise you a position. What I promise is the work, the measurement, and a report you can check yourself in Search Console. 02 

## What I actually change on a site so it ranks locally

 Locality goes into the titles and the headings, so a page about a Sevenoaks business says Sevenoaks where Google reads first. JSON-LD business schema carries the real address and the towns you serve. Breadcrumb schema tells a crawler where each page sits, and FAQ schema turns your real questions into results. The sitemap gets true dates, not placeholders. The robots.txt names all 15 AI crawlers, so the assistants that answer questions are allowed to read you. Two files, llms.txt and llms-full.txt, give those assistants the plain facts about the business in your own words. Canonical tags settle which page gets the credit. Reviews are the ones real customers wrote. I never fabricate a rating, and I will not add a star widget that the reviews do not support. 03 

## The Google Business Profile most businesses never finish

 Most profiles were set up once, years ago, and left. The name is right and the phone number is right, and everything else is blank or stale. The finished version has the right categories and the services listed one by one. It has the real photographs of the shop, the team and the work. It has weekly posts, so Google sees a business that is open. It has reviews from real customers, answered. And it carries the one link that matters most: the booking or ordering link, so a search becomes an appointment without a detour. 04 

## A Sevenoaks restaurant, 29 days, zero ad spend

 7 Oaks Grill had strong word of mouth and no online presence. I built an Instagram content system and did the Google Business Profile work. In 29 days the account reached 28,000+ accounts and produced 71,583 views, with zero paid advertising. Persa London, a Bromley studio making hand-painted leather, is the same idea on a marketplace. 25+ keyword-researched listing rewrites and 240 product variations on eBay took the shop to the top 5 percent of its UK category, with 61,515 impressions in 30 days and a 35.9 percent improvement in conversion rate. Both numbers come from the platforms' own dashboards, not from me. 05 

## What takes weeks, and what I will not promise

 Schema, sitemaps and crawler files take an afternoon and show up in Search Console within days. The profile work compounds over weeks. Rankings move when Google decides they move. I will not promise a position, a date, or a number of leads. I will show you the Search Console data, the impressions, the clicks and the positions, and you can read it without me in the room. 06 

## How it starts

 The free website audit is at conversionforge.co.uk/free-audit. I look at your site, your schema, your sitemap and your Google Business Profile, and I send you what is working and what is missing. If you want the work done, you email hello@weareconversionforge.uk and we agree the scope. There is no account manager. There is me, and you will always know who did the work. FAQ

 Do I need a new website for this? Usually not; most sites need the right structure and files added to what is already there, and I check yours before suggesting anything bigger. How long before I see results? The technical changes show in Search Console within days; ranking and profile changes take weeks, and I say which is which before we start. # Google Ads and Meta Ads Management for Small Businesses · Conversion Forge
URL: https://conversionforge.co.uk/services/google-ads-meta-ads-management

Google Ads and Meta Ads Management for Small Businesses · Conversion Forge 

 Service 

## Ads measured in bookings, watched every four hours, decided on dates.

 Facebook, Instagram and Google Ads for small businesses: one campaign, real bookings as the scoreboard, a watcher every four hours, and decisions on dated review points. Get the free audit or email Tk Based in Sevenoaks Handed over, yours to keep Kent, London and further conversionforge.co.uk/services Illustration, generated for this site 4 hours between every reading of a live campaign 3 instruments: the platform, the pixel and your own record 0 changes made to a live campaign without a human hand 01 

## Why most small-business ads measure the wrong thing

 Clicks are cheap to count and easy to report. They are also not what you sell. A dance class sells a child in the room. A restaurant sells a table booked. A barber sells a chair filled. Most small-business ad reports stop at the click, because that is what the platform shows first. I do not. Before a pound is spent, the outcome that actually matters is defined, measured and test-fired. The honest limitation comes first: ads cannot fix a booking page that does not work. I check the destination on a phone before the first pound goes out, and I have found dead booking buttons on live sites more than once. 02 

## The scoreboard is a booking, not a click

 Before any spend, the outcome event, a booking, an order or a call, is created on your pixel and test-fired, so the platform learns towards the thing you sell. Then there are three instruments, not one: the platform's count, the pixel's count, and your own record, the calendar, the till or the hall register. When the three agree, the numbers are real. When they disagree, that is the first thing I investigate, before anyone celebrates. The campaign itself is simple on purpose. One campaign, one ad set, two or three creatives. The copy is held identical, so the creative is the only variable and the test measures one thing. 03 

## What the system watches, and how often

 A read-only system polls the live campaign every four hours and logs every reading. It applies fixed rules: delivery, pacing, cost per booking against your own target, frequency, click-through trend and placement waste. Then it posts a plain-English digest. It changes nothing on its own. It cannot. Every change to a live campaign is a human hand, mine, with the rollback named before the change is made. That means you are never reading a report written from memory. You are reading what the campaign did, on the record, every four hours. 04 

## Decisions on dates, never on a whim

 On launch day the decision points go in the calendar: the five-day read, the event day, and the day after. The minimum evidence for any change is written down before launch, so nobody moves the goalposts once the numbers arrive. No creative is switched off on 24 hours of data. Budgets are never moved mid-learning. A campaign that is left alone long enough to be measured is a campaign you can learn from. 05 

## What I will not do with your money

 I will not launch to a page I have not checked on a phone. I will not switch creative because a day looked quiet. I will not move a budget while the platform is still learning. I will not report clicks as if they were customers. If the numbers say the campaign is not working, I will say so on the dated review, and I will say what I would change and why. 06 

## Who this suits

 This suits a small business with something bookable: a class, a table, a chair, a slot. It suits an owner who keeps their own record of bookings and is willing to share it, because that record is the third instrument. It suits a budget that is real but modest, where every pound needs to be watched and no pound can be wasted on guesswork. FAQ 

## Questions people ask

 What counts as a result? A booking, an order or a call, measured on your pixel and checked against your own calendar or till, never a click. How often will I hear from you? The watcher posts a plain-English digest every four hours, and the decisions happen on the dates set on launch day. What if my booking page is broken? I check it on a phone before any spend; if it fails, the ads do not run until it is fixed. Will you change things without telling me? No; the system only reports, every change is made by hand with the rollback named, and you see the digest. Why not let the platform optimise itself? It does, inside the campaign; what it cannot do is decide whether your business is winning, and that decision stays with a person on a date. How do I start? ## Where small-business leads actually come from

Your own website, with a form or a booking link that lands in your inbox. And outreach, sent on a fixed cadence, where every new thread starts with a human saying yes. I build all three so they work while you are working. The systems are yours when they are done. The honest limitation first: a lead is not a customer until they turn up. I measure to the booking, and I ask for your turn-up numbers, because that is where most small businesses leak. 02 

## Capture on your own site, not a rented form

 The form lives on your domain and delivers to your inbox or your phone. The list is yours. If a platform changes its terms or its prices, your leads do not go with it. There is nothing to log into and nothing to renew. A lead arrives as an email or a message, the way you already work. 03 

## Follow-up that happens without you

 Most leads go cold because nobody wrote back a second time. The follow-up sequence runs on days 3, 7, 14 and 21, and it stops the moment someone replies. Every message passes a plain-language check, so it reads like a person wrote it, because a person did. Sends are spaced so no inbox provider flags them. Nothing goes out on a new thread without a human approving the first message. 04

In each case the lead has a next action that the business can fulfil the same day. 05

 I can build the capture, the follow-up and the booking step. I cannot make people turn up. I measure to the booking and ask you for the turn-up numbers, and if the gap between the two is wide, that is the next thing we fix, together, not something I hide in a report. 06

 Case study 

## 7 Oaks Grill: word of mouth, put online.

 Case study: a Sevenoaks restaurant with strong word of mouth and no online presence reached 28,000+ accounts and 71,583 views in 29 days through an Instagram content system and Google Business Profile work. Get the free audit or email Tk Real client Numbers from the platforms No fee figures instagram.com · 7 Oaks Grill From the reel made for 7 Oaks Grill 71,583 views in 29 days 28,000+ accounts reached £0 spent on paid advertising 01 

## The business before

 7 Oaks Grill is a restaurant in Sevenoaks, Kent. It had what most restaurants would trade a great deal for: strong word of mouth. People who had eaten there told other people. What it did not have was any online presence. No account posting the food, no profile finished on Google. The recommendation stopped at the person who made it. 02 

## What was built

 Two things, both on the restaurant's own accounts. An Instagram content system, planned, filmed and posted in cycles so there was always something new without the owner thinking about it. And Google Business Profile optimisation, so the search a recommended diner makes next lands on the right result. No paid advertising was used at any point. That was the test: could the word of mouth be put online without buying reach. 03 

## The numbers, from the platforms

 In 29 days the account reached 28,000+ accounts and the posts produced 71,583 views. Zero was spent on ads. Those figures are from the platforms' own dashboards and can be checked against a screenshot. I did not calculate them and I do not round them up. 04 

## What it took from the owner

 Filming windows were agreed around service, never during it. A restaurant's time is its service, and the content system was built to take from the edges of the day, not the middle. The owner's part was to open the door at the agreed time and keep cooking. 05 

## What I would do next

 The views are the top of a funnel. The next step is to measure the bottom of it: how many of those views became tables, which means a booking or reservation step on the profile and the site that can be counted. Reach is proven. Bookings are the number that pays the rent, and that is what I would build to next. FAQ 

## Questions people ask

## Pilates Realm: booked from a page she owns, built from Kent.

 Case study: a Toronto Pilates instructor moved off a website builder to pilatesrealm.com, with a booking flow, her own prices and photographs, and the AI-search foundations. Built and launched remotely. Get the free audit or email Tk Real client Numbers from the platforms No fee figures pilatesrealm.com The live site, captured 13 September 2026 70 Canadian dollars a session, her own public price 2 faults caught in a sweep before launch 1 hour the old site lingers on the machine that made the change 01 

## The business before

 Pilates Realm offers private, duet and online Pilates in Toronto with a STOTT PILATES certified instructor, from CAD 70 a session, her own public price. The site sat on a website builder, on the builder's terms. The instructor did not own the domain the site lived on, and the pages could not be built to be found the way a local search needs. 02 

## What was built

 A site she owns at pilatesrealm.com , with a booking flow, her own prices, her biography and her own photographs. The search and AI-search foundations that every site I build ships with, so a search for Pilates in her part of the world can find her and an AI assistant can read her facts in her words. Delivered remotely from Kent, without a single in-person meeting. 03 

## The go-live, checked from a second machine

 Pointing a domain at a new site is the moment that matters, and it has a trap. The machine that makes the change keeps seeing the old site for up to an hour, because its own address book has not caught up yet. So the go-live was verified from a second machine, on a different network, reading the server's own headers and the page title, not a status code. Only when that machine saw the new site was it reported live. 04 

## What was fixed that nobody had noticed

 Two things, both found by a sweep of every sentence and every script before launch. A demonstration disclaimer that would have appeared on every live page, left over from the review build. And a booking confirmation email that carried a placeholder phone number, which real clients would have received. Neither would have shown up in a design review. Both would have been the first thing a new client saw. That sweep is now part of every launch. 05 

## What I would do next

 Search Console, then the booking count. The foundations are in; the next step is reading what Google does with them over the coming weeks and finishing her Google Business Profile with the booking link on it, so the search becomes a session without a detour. SAID 

## In their words

 “This is looking stupid good!!” Pilates Realm, Toronto · WhatsApp, 2 September 2026, first look at the new site “I like the site you created for me better.” Pilates Realm, Toronto · WhatsApp, 4 September 2026, after comparing it with another studio's site FAQ 

## Questions people ask

 What does Pilates Realm offer? Private, duet and online Pilates in Toronto with a STOTT PILATES certified instructor, from CAD 70 a session. What changed? The site moved off a website builder to pilatesrealm.com , a domain she owns, with a booking flow, her prices, biography and photographs. How was the launch checked? From a second machine on a different network, reading the server's own headers and the page title, because the machine that makes a change still sees the old site for up to an hour. What was caught before launch? A demonstration disclaimer on every page and a placeholder phone number inside the booking confirmation email, both removed. Was any of this done in person? No; the whole build was delivered remotely from Kent. Could you do this for my studio? Yes; request the free audit at conversionforge.co.uk/free-audit or email hello@weareconversionforge.uk . # Warriorz Performing Arts Academy, Stevenage: a dance school website, 28 classes on one timetable · Conversion Forge
URL: https://conversionforge.co.uk/work/warriorz-performing-arts-academy

Warriorz Performing Arts Academy, Stevenage: a dance school website, 28 classes on one timetable · Conversion Forge 

 Case study 

## Warriorz: twenty-eight classes, finally on one page.

 Case study: a Stevenage performing arts academy got a site built on its real 28-class timetable and its own photographs, with a hero film and phone-native media, live at warriorzperformingartsacademy.co.uk. Get the free audit or email Tk Real client Numbers from the platforms No fee figures warriorzperformingartsacademy.co.uk The live site, captured 13 September 2026 28 classes on one timetable page 390 pixel phone screen, measured before and after 1 booking system kept as the system of record 01 

## The business before

 Warriorz Performing Arts Academy in Stevenage teaches dance and performing arts to children and adults. Twenty-eight classes a week, each with its own day, time and age group. That timetable lived in the academy's booking system and in the heads of the people who ran it. A parent looking for a Tuesday class for a nine-year-old had no single page that answered the question. 02 

## What was built

 A site built on the academy's real 28-class timetable, so every class has its day, time and age group on one page. The academy's own photographs throughout, and a hero film so the first thing a visitor sees is the room and the movement, not a stock image of a studio. Live at warriorzperformingartsacademy.co.uk . 03 

## Built for the phone first

 Parents look for classes on a phone, usually while doing something else. So the film that opens the site was cut for a phone screen: a portrait poster and a small portrait loop, rather than a wide film squeezed into a tall frame. It was measured on a 390-pixel screen before and after, because a site that looks right on a laptop and wrong on a phone is wrong for most of its visitors. 04 

## What stayed the client's

 The academy's existing class-booking system stayed the system of record. The site wraps it and points to it; it never replaces it. A parent books where the academy already takes bookings, and nothing at the desk changed. That is a rule I keep. The client's working system is the truth, and the site serves it. 05 

## What I would do next

 Local search, because a class is found by town. The page already carries Stevenage in the right places; the next step is the Google Business Profile finished with the booking link, and then reading Search Console to see which class names people search for, so the timetable page answers those first. FAQ 

## Questions people ask

 What does the site show? All 28 classes with their day, time and age group, on the academy's real timetable, with its own photographs and a hero film. Where do bookings go? To the academy's existing class-booking system, which stayed the system of record. Why the phone-first film? Because parents look for classes on a phone; the opener is a portrait poster and a small portrait loop, measured on a 390-pixel screen. Where is the academy? Stevenage, and the site is live at warriorzperformingartsacademy.co.uk . Did the academy have to change anything? No; the site wraps the booking system it already used. # Shepherd-Prince, Kent: a kitchen and bathroom fitter's website from 1,231 photographs · Conversion Forge
URL: https://conversionforge.co.uk/work/shepherd-prince

Shepherd-Prince, Kent: a kitchen and bathroom fitter's website from 1,231 photographs · Conversion Forge 

 Case study 

## Shepherd-Prince: twenty-three years of fitted rooms, twenty-nine photographs.

 Case study: a Kent kitchen and bathroom fitter. A brand kit and a page built from 29 photographs chosen from the 1,231 he owned, delivered in the week his agreement promised. Get the free audit or email Tk Real client Numbers from the platforms No fee figures Case study Rooms fitted by Shepherd-Prince, from his own photographs 1,231 photographs the client owned 29 chosen, each looked at full size 1 dated promise in the agreement, met 01 

## The business before

 Shepherd-Prince is a family business fitting kitchens and bathrooms across Kent. Twenty-three years of fitted rooms, and the evidence of it sat in a phone: photographs of finished work, hundreds of them, seen by nobody but the person who took them. The trade needed a page that showed the rooms at the size a customer would judge them, with a number to call. 02 

## The photographs

 The client owned 1,231 unique photographs across two folders. Every candidate was looked at at full size, not as a thumbnail, and 29 were chosen. Looking at full size is where the work was. A phone's watermark burned into the corner of a shot, and a photographer's feet at the bottom of another, were both caught and excluded at that stage. On a thumbnail sheet neither is visible; on a customer's screen both would have been. 03 

## What was built

 A brand kit, so the name looks the same on the page, the van and the invoice. And a site page for the trade, with the services listed, the 29 photographs at full size, and a mobile number that goes to the person who fits the rooms. 04 

## A promise with a date on it

 The agreement carried one dated obligation: the page within the first week after the first payment, once the photographs had arrived. It was met. A date in an agreement is a promise, and I treat it as one. It goes in the calendar the day the agreement is signed, and the work is finished against it. 05 

## What I would do next

 Reviews and local search. A fitter is chosen on trust, and trust online is real reviews from real customers with the town in them. The next step is a Google Business Profile with the photographs on it, the reviews gathered properly, and the page built out so "kitchen fitter" plus the town lands on Shepherd-Prince. FAQ 

## Questions people ask

 What does Shepherd-Prince do? Kitchen and bathroom fitting across Kent, a family business. How were the photographs chosen? 29 were chosen from the 1,231 the client owned, every candidate looked at full size, with a phone watermark and a photographer's feet caught and excluded. What was built? A brand kit and a site page with the services listed, the photographs at full size and a mobile number. Was the deadline met? Yes; the agreement promised the page within the first week after the first payment once the photographs arrived, and it was delivered in that week. Why look at every photograph at full size? Because the flaws that put a customer off, a watermark or a stray foot, do not show on a thumbnail. Could you do this for my trade?
